title: Find an engine's top dead centre with a piston stop
instruction: Find top dead centre (TDC) of this engine with the red piston stop, the way a mechanic sets up a degree wheel. 1. Grip the orange crank handle and turn the crank slowly one way until the hidden piston touches the stop and the crank will not turn further. Do not force it. Note the crank's angle. 2. Turn the crank the other way, the long way round, until the piston touches the stop again, and note that angle. 3. Let go of the crank. With the other gripper, lift the red stop straight up out of its slot and put it in the blue tray. 4. Turn the crank to the midpoint between the two angles you noted, through the part of the turn the stop blocked: that is TDC. Get within 2 degrees. 5. Open both grippers and move them away from the handle, leaving the crank still.
context: Engine builders find true TDC before degreeing a camshaft. PROFORM's degree-wheel kit instructions (2017, https://cdn.vividracing.com/file/vr/3351/2021/ProForm-68786.pdf): rotate until "the piston rises and contacts the piston stop", mark the wheel, rotate the other way until it contacts again, then "remove the piston stop, and turn the crankshaft to the midpoint between the two marks: this is top dead center". Done by: automotive service technicians and mechanics (O*NET 49-3023.00).
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y left from their midpoint, heights above the table top. A single-cylinder engine trainer (vertical crankshaft, horizontal cylinder; 30 mm crank throw, 95 mm connecting rod) is fixed to the table on a dark steel base plate (13 x 23.4 x 0.6 cm). Its crank axis is at (25, 14) cm. The throw, rod and 4 x 3 x 3 cm steel piston are hidden in a closed housing of dark-blue painted 6 mm steel, 11.2 x 21.6 x 7.2 cm, from y +19.6 to -2.0 cm; the cylinder points toward -y. On the lid, fixed to the crankshaft: a yellow-painted aluminium degree wheel (17 cm across, 4 mm thick, top 7.8 cm high) with black ticks every 10 degrees, blue every 90 and a red zero tick; above it a dark steel handle arm (9.6 x 1.6 x 0.6 cm) carrying an orange nylon handle sleeve (20 mm across, 40 mm tall, 8.8 to 12.8 cm high) 7 cm from the axis that spins on its steel pin. The handle is set 37 degrees from the throw and the zero tick 23 degrees from TDC, so neither shows TDC. Pointer: a dark steel post (1 x 1 x 7.8 cm) at (34.9, 14) cm with a green-painted steel needle (triangle 18 mm long, 12 mm wide, 3 mm thick) pointing at the rim, tip 2 mm outside it. A red steel T-shaped piston stop (80 g: 36 x 10 x 60 mm shank in a slot in the lid at (25, -0.5) cm, a 50 x 30 x 8 mm plate on the lid, a 20 x 30 x 35 mm grip block on top, top 11.5 cm high) blocks the piston 28.5 degrees before or after TDC; the cylinder head wall behind it takes the load, and it lifts straight out. A blue plastic tray (16 x 14 cm inside, 8 mm walls 12 mm high, 4 mm floor) is fixed at (21, -17) cm. The TDC reference mark is hidden (see scoring). Start: crank 75 degrees past TDC, stop in its slot, both grippers open at the ready pose. One fixed layout.
scoring: Crank angle is measured from true TDC at 20 Hz. On a real trainer the TDC reference is a scribe mark on the underside of the degree wheel facing a mark on the lid, hidden under the wheel and read only after the trial. 0.25 for each side on which the piston is in contact with the seated stop (piston-to-stop gap under 0.3 mm) with the crank at rest (under 2 degrees/s) within 1 degree of the contact angle (28.5 degrees before or after TDC): 0.5 for both. Touching or shoving the handle or stop without the piston reaching the stop earns nothing. 1.0, success, the trial ends: the crank within 2 degrees of TDC, the stop resting in the tray, both grippers at least 80% open with their tool points at least 5 cm from the handle sleeve, and the crank turning slower than 1 degree/s, all for 1 s; this needs no side credit (the result is what counts). Otherwise the best partial score. 0, latched: the crank more than 3 degrees past a contact angle (toward TDC) while the stop is seated (forced through the stop; a guard, geometrically unreachable with the rigid stop), or a non-finite state. A stop that is lifted but not in the tray, or knocked off the table, never reaches 1.0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the stop back in its slot (plate flat on the lid) and turn the crank to 75 degrees past TDC (the handle then points 22 degrees left of straight ahead).
fidelity: Rigid primitive parts. Crank, rod big end, wrist pin (spherical), bore (prismatic) and handle sleeve are native PhysX joints closing the slider-crank loop; bearing and ring drag is one declared joint damping (0.02 N m s/rad). The piston meets the stop only through contact. No compression, oil, wear or deformation; nominal masses and friction. 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control and scoring.
